subject: Elara Labs — capacity packaging, term options, and start-gate proposal
messages:
From: Ruth Chen <ruth.chen@elara.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike O'Neill <mike@elara.ai>, procurement@elara.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity packaging questions + target start window

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — Elara's engineering and product teams are aligned on moving forward with a Dedicated deployment. Before procurement drafts anything, I need clarity on a few items so we can square this with our finance team:

- GPU pool sizing: we expect a 95th-percentile sustained throughput equivalent to ~180k tokens/sec across inference (mix of short and long prompts). What GPU mix do you recommend (A100 v H100) for predictable performance?
- Commit term: our CFO leans toward 24 months but is open to 12 or 36 if the economics are compelling. We need the delta in unit pricing between 12/24/36 month reserved commits.
- Ramp/start gate: our infrastructure team cannot take capacity more than ~4 weeks before March 15 due to data center change freeze. Can Redwood support a delayed start gate with credits if the actual ramp begins after contract execution?
- SLA/throughput guarantees: procurement will push for a guaranteed throughput SLO (or a clear performance fallback) — what level of guarantee can you provide for reserved pools vs. burst capacity?

I've attached a short requirements spreadsheet with our callouts. Can you send a proposal with pricing bands and a preferred ramp schedule?

Ruth Chen
VP, Platform
Elara Labs

Attachment: Elara_Requirements_2026-02-08.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ruth Chen <ruth.chen@elara.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity packaging questions + target start window

Ruth — thanks for the clear requirements and the spreadsheet. High-level answers first, then a proposed set of options you can share with finance: 

1) Recommended GPU mix
- For a 95th-percentile sustained ~180k tokens/sec profile with mixed prompt lengths, we recommend a pool built around H100-class instances (best cost/perf at scale) with a small A100 reserve for consistency in long-sequence workloads. Rough starting configuration: 16 x H100 (NVLink) + 4 x A100 for KV-heavy, long-context tail. This gives you headroom for continuous batching and consistent latency.

2) Commit terms & delta (ballpark)
- 12 months: base unit price (1.00x)
- 24 months: ~15% unit discount vs 12m (0.85x)
- 36 months: ~21% unit discount vs 12m (0.79x)
These are starting points — we can layer additional credits for upfront payment or multi-quarter ramp commitments.

3) Ramp and start gate
- Standard: start = contract effective date, 8-week ramp to target capacity.
- Delayed-start option: we can contract now but schedule a start-gate (no resource allocation) up to 8 weeks post-signature. If Redwood cannot allocate capacity by the agreed start date through our planning process, we offer a one-time credit up to 8% of first-year committed spend.

4) Throughput SLA
- For reserved pools: target 95th-percentile latency and throughput SLO tied to a defined test harness (shared eval prompts). If SLO is missed due to Redwood cause (kernel scheduling, capacity misallocation), we provide service credits.
- Burst: best-effort; we can provide guaranteed burst capacity as an add-on for a price.

I've attached a short capacity summary PDF that maps these options to an estimated monthly spend range. Priyom is copied on this thread and will follow up with a technical note on batching parameters and observable counters we would include in the SLO.

Next step: is a packaged proposal with 24-month pricing and the delayed-start clause acceptable for procurement to review? If yes, we'll turn it into a draft SOW for legal.

— Jonas
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Capacity_Summary_Elara_20260206.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Ruth Chen <ruth.chen@elara.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Feb 2026 15:26:00 -0800
Subject: Technical note — throughput guarantees, observability, and pool sizing

Ruth — quick technical follow-up to clarify how we define the SLO and operationalize the ramp: 

- Measurement harness: we run a shared benchmark using your representative prompt set (we'll use the spreadsheet samples). Throughput SLOs will be measured as sustained token/sec over configurable windows and 95th-percentile tail latency for 4k and 32k contexts.
- Autoscaling: reserved pool is configured with a target steady-state capacity and a headroom buffer (10–15%) for small spikes. For larger burst requirements, we either route to a paid burst pool (pre-warmed) or fall back to a multi-tier model with lighter quantized variants.
- Minimum contiguous commit: operationally, we ask for a minimum 2-quarter contiguous commitment inside the reserved term to justify pre-warming specific instance types; we can include a clause that allows minor reductions at quarter boundaries with 30 days notice.
- Ramp profile: we typically use a 4-8 week linear ramp (week-by-week capacity add). Given your March 15 freeze, we suggest a contract executed in February, start gate March 1, 2-week staging, full ramp complete by March 29. If the freeze pushes your production start beyond March 15, we will hold capacity in a warm state and apply the delayed-start credit Jonas mentioned.

I'll enumerate the exact counters we'll expose in the console (token/sec, mean latency, 95/99p tails, batch sizes, cache hit-rate). Happy to sync with your infra team for a short runbook call.

— Priyom
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ruth Chen <ruth.chen@elara.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike O'Neill <mike@elara.ai>, procurement@elara.ai, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity packaging questions + target start window

Thanks — helpful detail. A couple of points from procurement/finance after reviewing the numbers: 

- Term: CFO prefers 24 months but would entertain 36 months if Redwood can move to a blended discount of ~22% vs the 12-month baseline and include a one-time implementation credit to offset our migration work.
- Start: we cannot accept a start earlier than March 1 (data center freeze), and prefer start no later than March 15. If Redwood holds capacity idle on our behalf past March 15, we will require a pro-rated credit for the idle weeks.
- SLA: procurement is likely to accept a throughput SLO tied to the shared harness but wants a clear remediation ladder and an uptime / performance credit schedule in the SOW.

I've attached our detailed requirements spreadsheet (token mix by endpoint, peak windows). Can you produce a commercial term sheet that shows: 24m vs 36m blended pricing, a one-time implementation credit line, and explicit language for delayed-start credits?

Ruth
VP, Platform
Elara Labs

Attachment: Elara_Requirements_2026-02-08.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ruth Chen <ruth.chen@elara.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Mike O'Neill <mike@elara.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity packaging questions + target start window

On Sun, Feb 8, 2026 at 11:03 AM Ruth Chen <ruth.chen@elara.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — helpful detail. A couple of points from procurement/finance after reviewing the numbers: ...

Ruth — appreciate the clarity. Below is a single-sheet commercial proposal we believe addresses procurement's asks and keeps the ramp predictable for both teams. If this looks good, we'll generate a draft SOW and send via DocuSign for signature.

Proposed commercial summary (high level):
- Structure: 24-month reserved commit (preferred) with option to convert to 36m at the end of year one with a retroactive blended credit if exercised within the first 90 days.
- GPU pool: 16 x H100 + 4 x A100 (dedicated pool). Pricing reflects full stack (inference runtime, monitoring, 24x7 support).
- Discount: 24m list discount = 18% vs 12m baseline. For a sealed 24m+36m conversation we can move to 22% blended (requires early commitment language).
- Implementation credit: one-time credit equal to 3% of the first-year committed spend to help cover migration/setup costs.
- Delayed-start / idle-capacity clause: start gate no earlier than Mar 1, 2026; if Redwood is unable to bring the pool to your environment by Mar 15 through our planning, Redwood will apply a pro-rated credit for idle weeks up to 8 weeks (credit cap = 8% of year-one committed spend). If you request we hold capacity idle beyond Mar 15 for business reasons, we will bill a minimal warm-standby fee (negotiable) unless a separate pre-funded hold is agreed.
- SLA & remediation: throughput SLO tied to the shared harness; service credits escalate by severity (1% of monthly committed spend per missed SLO bucket, up to 8% monthly cap). Exact buckets and measurement windows will be in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) If procurement agrees to the 18% at 24m with the 3% implementation credit, we'll draft SOW with the delayed-start language and SLO appendix.
2) Legal review on both sides (we'll include the ramp schedule and test harness in an addendum).
3) DocuSign via the link below if you approve — target execution week of Feb 16 to allow staging and a March 1 start gate.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABC-ELARA-20260210
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/EL-2387

I'll loop in Lauren (commercial counsel) and Priyom for the SLO appendix. Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow if you want to close the numbers.

— Jonas
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Draft_SOW_Elara_20260210.pdf
